title: A smooth hypersurface germ realizes any tangent hyperplane
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $Y$ be a smooth separated geometrically integral finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $p\in Y(k)$ [def-pc-rational-point]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Suppose $d=\dim Y\ge2$, with dimension as in [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $H\subset T_{Y/k,p}$ be a codimension-one $k$-linear subspace of the tangent space [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space]. There are an open neighbourhood $V\subseteq Y$ of $p$ and a closed immersion $j:D\hookrightarrow V$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion], where $D$ is smooth, separated, geometrically integral and of finite type over $k$, with $\dim D=d-1$, and a point $q\in D(k)$ mapping to $p$, such that the tangent map of $D\to Y$ identifies $T_{D/k,q}$ with $H$.

source.place: Chapter I Lemma 3.6, printed p.18, proof: hyperplane H through P not containing Tgt_P(V); shrink the unique component through P to its smooth neighbourhood. Algebraic justification: Stacks algebra.tex Tag 00NQ, lemma-regular-ring-CM; Tag 00TV, lemma-separable-smooth; morphisms.tex Tag 01V9, lemma-smooth-at-point; varieties.tex Tag 038X, lemma-geometrically-regular-smooth. The hyperplane in this statement is the intersection of Milne's ambient hyperplane with Tgt_P(V).

proof.text: Choose an affine chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ containing $p$ from a finite affine finite-type cover supplied by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Thus $A$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra, as also expressed by [lem-pc-affine-finite-type-algebra]. Geometric integrality implies that $Y$, hence its nonempty affine open $U$, is integral, so $A$ is a domain. The point gives a surjective evaluation $A\to k$, with maximal kernel $\mathfrak p$. Put $R=\mathcal O_{Y,p}=A_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pR$, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization]. Smoothness gives regularity of $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular]. Also $\dim R=\dim A=\dim U=\dim Y=d$: use [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-local-ring-localization], [lem-weil-pbc-spec-topological-krull-dimension-ring] and [lem-sc-integral-locally-algebraic-opens-dimension].

source.place: Tag 0A21, lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic (3), together with Algebra Tag 00OS, lemma-dimension-spell-it-out, and Varieties Tag 056S, lemma-smooth-regular

proof.text: Write $E=\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension], $\dim_k E=d$. The identification [lem-sc-rational-point-tangent-derivation-identification] gives $T_{Y/k,p}=E^\vee$. Choose a nonzero functional $L:E^\vee\to k$ whose kernel is $H$, by choosing a basis of $H$ and extending it by one vector. In a basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ of $E$, put $v=\sum_i L(e_i^\vee)e_i$. Then $L(\lambda)=\lambda(v)$ for every $\lambda\in E^\vee$, and $v\ne0$. Lift $v$ through the quotient map $\mathfrak m\to E$ to $f\in\mathfrak m$. Thus $f\notin\mathfrak m^2$, and the annihilator of its class in $E^\vee$ is exactly $H$.

source.place: Tag 0B2E, lemma-tangent-space-rational-point; elementary finite-dimensional double-dual calculation

proof.text: Represent $f=a/s$ with $a\in A$, $s\in A\setminus\mathfrak p$, by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization]. Since the residue of $f$ is zero and $s(p)\ne0$, one has $a\in\mathfrak p$. Replace $U$ by the principal open $D(s)=\operatorname{Spec}A_s$, using [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], and replace $A$ by $A_s$. This ring is still finite type, as adjoining $s^{-1}$ amounts to adding one generator with relation $sT-1=0$. Now $f$ is the germ of the actual section $a/s\in A$; call this section $h$. Its germ and its cotangent class are exactly the chosen $f$ and $v$.

Extend the nonzero class of $f$ to a basis $[f],[f_2],\ldots,[f_d]$ of $E$. Lift the remaining basis vectors to $\mathfrak m$. Nakayama [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators], applied to the finitely generated $R$-module $\mathfrak m$, shows that $f,f_2,\ldots,f_d$ minimally generate $\mathfrak m$. The regular-parameter theorem [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], with $c=1$, gives that $R/(f)$ is regular local of dimension $d-1$.

source.place: Tag 00DV, lemma-NAK (4); Tag 00NQ, lemma-regular-ring-CM, with c=1

proof.text: Let $Z=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B=A/(h)$, the zero scheme of $h$, a closed subscheme of $U$ by [lem-pc-zero-scheme-properties]. The point $p$ factors through a point $z\in Z(k)$ because $h(p)=0$. The quotient-localization isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient] identifies $\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ with $R/(f)$, with its quotient map from $R$ and unchanged residue field $k$. Apply [lem-sfb-regular-separable-affine-smooth-neighbourhood] to the affine scheme $Z$, its finite-type algebra $B$, and this prime. Regularity was proved in step 4; its residue extension is the identity $k/k$, hence finite separable. Obtain $b\in B$ with $b(z)\ne0$ such that $Z_b=\operatorname{Spec}B_b$ is smooth over $k$. Lift $b$ to $t\in A$. Then $Z_b$ is the zero scheme of $h$ inside $U_t$, since $(A/(h))_b=A_t/(h)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-quotient-commute].

source.place: Tag 00TV, lemma-separable-smooth; Tag 00CT, proposition-localize-quotient; Schemes Tag 01I3, lemma-standard-open-affine

proof.text: The affine finite-type scheme $Z_b$ is smooth, so [lem-wf-smooth-components-disjoint] says its irreducible components are disjoint and open and closed. Let $C$ be the unique component containing $z$. Choose a principal open $D(c)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}B_b$ with $z\in D(c)\subseteq C$. This basis argument is direct from the Zariski topology: if $C$ is open and its complement is $V(I)$, choose $c\in I$ outside the prime $z$. Lift $c$ to $u\in A_t$ through the quotient $A_t\to B_b$. Set $V=(U_t)_u$ and $D=(Z_b)_c$. Principal localization and quotient commute, so $D=\operatorname{Spec}(\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)/(h))$ is closed in the affine open $V\subseteq Y$. It contains the same $k$-point $q=z$. It is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes]. Its space is irreducible, being a nonempty open in $C$. Every stalk of $D$ is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular], hence a domain by [lem-sc-regular-local-domain]. In particular every nilpotent section vanishes in every stalk, hence vanishes; $D$ is reduced. By [def-pc-integral-scheme], reducedness and irreducibility show that $D$ is integral.

source.place: Chapter I Lemma 3.6, printed p.18: the unique component through the nonsingular point; Stacks algebra.tex Tag 00NP, lemma-regular-domain, for reducedness

proof.text: Write $D=\operatorname{Spec}F$. Its coordinate ring is a quotient of a ring obtained from the finite-type $k$-algebra $A$ by two principal localizations, so it is generated by the images of the generators of $A$ together with two inverse elements. Thus $D$ is finite type. An affine $k$-scheme is separated directly: [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies its self-product with $\operatorname{Spec}(F\otimes_kF)$, and its diagonal is induced by the surjective multiplication map $F\otimes_kF\to F$, $x\otimes y\mapsto xy$, and so is a closed immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The local ring at $q$ is still $R/(f)$; localization at elements nonzero at $q$ does not change the stalk. As $F$ is a finite-type domain and $q$ has residue field $k$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-local-ring-localization] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-topological-krull-dimension-ring] give $\dim D=\dim\mathcal O_{D,q}=d-1$.

source.place: Tag 00OS, lemma-dimension-spell-it-out; Schemes Tag 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes, for the explicit multiplication description

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak n$ be the maximal ideal of $R/(f)=\mathcal O_{D,q}$, and let $\iota:D\to Y$ be $j$ followed by the open immersion $V\subseteq Y$; by steps 5--7 its stalk map $\iota^\sharp_q:R\to R/(f)$ is the quotient map. Its cotangent space is $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2=\mathfrak m/(\mathfrak m^2+(f))=E/kv$. Indeed the image of $rf$ modulo $\mathfrak m^2$ is $r(p)v$, and all multiples of $v$ occur. So $\iota^\sharp_q$ induces the quotient $u:E\to E/kv$. Apply [lem-sc-rational-point-tangent-derivation-identification] to $D$ at $q$ and to $Y$ at $p$, both with residue field $k$: $\theta\mapsto\ell_\theta$ identifies $T_{D/k,q}$ with $(E/kv)^\vee$, and $\eta\mapsto\ell_\eta$ identifies $T_{Y/k,p}$ with $E^\vee$, the identification used in step 2. By [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space] the tangent map sends $\theta$ to $\iota\circ\theta$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-stalk-map-composition](b) $(\iota\circ\theta)^\sharp=\theta^\sharp\circ\iota^\sharp_q$, with the same germ isomorphism of $k[\epsilon]$ on both sides. Since $\iota^\sharp_q$ preserves residues, comparing $\epsilon$-coefficients gives $D_{\iota\circ\theta}=D_\theta\circ\iota^\sharp_q$, hence $\ell_{\iota\circ\theta}=\ell_\theta\circ u$. Thus under these identifications the tangent map is precomposition with $u$. It is injective because $u$ is surjective, and its image is the set of functionals on $E$ vanishing at $v$, which is exactly the hyperplane $H$ of step 2. Thus the required tangent identification holds, with both residue fields equal to $k$.

source.place: Tag 0B2E, lemma-tangent-space-rational-point; Tag 0B2F, lemma-map-tangent-spaces; elementary cotangent quotient calculation

proof.text: Finally $D$ is geometrically integral. For every finite field extension $L/k$, each element of $L$ is algebraic over the algebraically closed field $k$, so it belongs to the image of $k$; hence $k\to L$ is an isomorphism. Consequently $F\otimes_kL\cong F$ is a domain. The finite-field-extension test [lem-per-geometric-integrality-finite-field-test] now shows that $F\otimes_kK$ is a domain for every field extension $K/k$. Since $D_K=\operatorname{Spec}(F\otimes_kK)$, this is precisely geometric integrality as defined in [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. All localizations retained $q$, so $p\in V$ and $q$ maps to $p$.
